1.theory:
## What CSS is CSS — **Cascading Style Sheets**. The **styling** language. HTML describes **structure**, CSS describes **appearance**: colors, fonts, spacing, layout. ## Why not in HTML In the past styles were written directly in HTML: ``. That is bad: - Styles mix with structure. - Change appearance — edit every page. - Huge HTML. CSS is separate. One style file — the whole site. ## Cascade **Cascade** — rules apply by priority. Multiple rules for one element — the "stronger" one wins (specificity, order, `!important`). Hence the name. ## Example ```html

Text

With CSS — blue, 20px. ## What can be styled - Text and background colors - Size, font, weight - Spacing and borders - Layout (blocks, flexbox, grid) - Animations, transitions - And much more ## CSS does not replace HTML or JS - HTML — structure - CSS — appearance - JS — behavior Without HTML there is nothing to style. Without CSS the site works but looks like a 1995 document. ## What if - Style a non-existent element — the rule simply does not apply. - Forget `;` after a property — the rule may not work. ## Common mistake Writing styles directly in HTML via `style="..."`. 3.title: Syntax: Rules, Selector, Property
3.theory:
## Rule structure

```css
selector {
  property: value;
  property: value;
}
```

Example:

```css
p {
  color: red;
  font-size: 16px;
}
```

## Breakdown

- `p` — **selector**, whom to style
- `color: red;` — **declaration**: `property: value;`
- `{ }` — rule block
- `;` — end of declaration, **mandatory**

## Multiple selectors

```css
h1, h2, h3 {
  color: navy;
}
```

One rule — for three tags. Comma-separated.

## Nested styles (do not work)

CSS does not support nesting like SASS. `p { span { ... } }` — will not work. Only via combined selectors (lesson 5).

## Comments

```css
/* This is a comment */
```

`//` **does not work** in CSS (unlike JS). Only `/* */`.

## What if

- Forget `;` after a declaration — CSS may skip the rule.
- Forget `{ }` — rule not recognized.
- `//` instead of `/* */` — error.

## Common mistake

`// comment` — habit from JS. In CSS — only `/* */`.

## Summary

- `selector { property: value; }`
- Multiple selectors — comma-separated
- `;` after each declaration
- Comments — `/* */`

6.title: Pseudo-classes: :hover, :focus
6.theory:
## What a pseudo-class is

A pseudo-class is a state of an element. `:hover` — cursor over, `:focus` — focused (after click / Tab).

## :hover

```css
button:hover {
  background: blue;
}
```

Applies when the mouse is over the button.

## :focus

```css
input:focus {
  border-color: blue;
  outline: none;
}
```

When the field receives focus (clicked or Tab).

## :active

```css
a:active {
  color: red;
}
```

At the moment of pressing (between mousedown and mouseup).

## :visited

```css
a:visited {
  color: purple;
}
```

Visited link.

## Order for links

`LVHA`: `:link`, `:visited`, `:hover`, `:active`. Otherwise some states override.

## What if

- Forget `:` — `hover { }` does not work.
- `:hover` on mobile — works on tap with a delay, not always.

## Common mistake

`:hover` without a base style. Without `button { ... }` and `button:hover { ... }` the transition is abrupt.

## Summary

- `:hover` — hover
- `:focus` — focus
- `:active` — press
- `:visited` — visited
- Order LVHA for links

7.title: Selector Specificity
7.theory:
## What specificity is If two rules claim one element, the "stronger" applies. Strength — **specificity**. ## Weights - Tag (`p`) — 1 - Class (`.x`) — 10 - id (`#x`) — 100 - Inline (`style=`) — 1000 The bigger the sum — the stronger. ## Example ```css p { color: red; } /* 1 */ .text { color: blue; } /* 10 */ #main { color: green; } /* 100 */ ``` `

` — green, since id beats all. ## Order If specificity is equal — the **last** rule wins: ```css p { color: red; } p { color: blue; } ``` Blue (second). ## !important ```css p { color: red !important; } ``` Beats everything except another `!important`. **Avoid** — breaks the cascade. ## Practice - Style via classes — predictable. - id for CSS — rarely, high specificity. - `!important` — almost never. ## What if - `#x` beats `.x`. Confusing. - `!important` everywhere — cascade broken, cannot change. ## Common mistake `!important` to "just make it work". Better — understand specificity. ## Summary - id > class > tag > universal - Inline — strongest of all - On equal — last rule - `!important` — avoid

8.title: Colors: color and background
8.theory:
## color — text color

```css
p { color: red; }
```

Changes text color.

## background — background

```css
p { background: yellow; }
```

Shorthand. Full — `background-color`, `background-image`, etc.

## Ways to set color

1. **Name**: `red`, `blue`, `navy`, `tomato` — 140+ names.
2. **HEX**: `#ff0000`, `#333`, `#007bff`.
3. **rgb / rgba**: `rgb(255, 0, 0)`, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`.
4. **hsl / hsla**: `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`.

## HEX

`#RRGGBB`. `#f00` = `#ff0000` (short form if characters pair up).

- `#000000` — black
- `#ffffff` — white
- `#808080` — gray

## rgba and transparency

```css
background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
```

Black at 50% transparency.

## What if

- `#ff` — invalid, need 3 or 6.
- `color: 255` — not a color, error.
- Typo `backgroud` — rule ignored.

## Common mistake

`background-color: #fff` without `#` — `fff` is not a color. With `#`.

## Summary

- `color` — text, `background` — background
- Name, HEX, rgb, hsl
- `rgba` — with transparency
- HEX — `#rrggbb` or `#rgb`

9.title: Fonts
9.theory:
## font-family

```css
body {
  font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
}
```

Comma-separated — list. Browser takes the first available. `sans-serif` — system "without serifs".

## font-size

```css
p { font-size: 16px; }
h1 { font-size: 2rem; }
```

Units: `px`, `rem` (from root), `em` (from parent), `%`. More in lesson 23.

## font-weight

```css
b { font-weight: bold; }        /* 700 */
p { font-weight: normal; }      /* 400 */
h1 { font-weight: 900; }        /* very bold */
```

Numbers 100–900, step 100.

## font-style

```css
em { font-style: italic; }
```

`normal` / `italic` / `oblique`.

## Loading a custom font

```css
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto');
body { font-family: 'Roboto', sans-serif; }
```

Or via `<link>` in HTML. Requires internet — does not work offline.

## What if

- `font-family: "Roboto"` without loading — browser uses fallback.
- `font-size: 20` without units — error.
- Wrong name — fallback.

## Common mistake

Forgetting fallback: `font-family: "MyFont"` — if it does not load, serif by default. Always add `, sans-serif`.

## Summary

- `font-family` — list, comma-separated, with fallback
- `font-size` — size (px, rem)
- `font-weight` — 100–900
- `font-style` — italic / normal

10.title: Text Alignment and Spacing
10.theory:
## text-align

```css
h1 { text-align: center; }
p { text-align: justify; }
```

- `left` — left
- `right` — right
- `center` — center
- `justify` — justified

Works for **block** elements (text inside them).

## line-height

Line spacing:

```css
p { line-height: 1.5; }
```

Unitless — multiplier from `font-size`. `1.5` = 1.5 times the font. Standard for readability: 1.4–1.6.

`line-height: 24px` — fixed pixels. Worse — does not scale.

## letter-spacing

```css
h1 { letter-spacing: 2px; }
```

## text-indent

Paragraph indent:

```css
p { text-indent: 2em; }
```

## Why

- `text-align` — typography
- `line-height` — readability
- `letter-spacing` — accents

## What if

- `text-align: center` on inline (e.g. `<span>`) — does not work. Need a block parent.
- `line-height` too small (<1) — lines stick together.

## Common mistake

`line-height: 1.5px` — units, got 1.5 pixels. No units — multiplier.

## Summary

- `text-align` — left / right / center / justify
- `line-height` — 1.5 (no units)
- `letter-spacing` — between letters
- `text-indent` — paragraph indent

11.title: Text Styles
11.theory:
## text-decoration

```css
a { text-decoration: none; }
.underline { text-decoration: underline; }
.strike { text-decoration: line-through; }
```

Often — to remove link underlines.

## text-transform

```css
h1 { text-transform: uppercase; }
```

- `uppercase` — ALL CAPS
- `lowercase` — all lowercase
- `capitalize` — Every Word Capitalized
- `none` — as-is

## Fonts vs styles

Do not confuse:
- `font-weight: bold` — visual boldness
- `<strong>` in HTML — **meaning** "important"
- `text-transform` — visual case change (HTML stays as-is)

## white-space

```css
pre { white-space: pre; }
.nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }
```

- `nowrap` — no wrap
- `pre` — preserve spaces and newlines

## text-shadow

```css
h1 { text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); }
```

Offset X, Y, blur, color.

## What if

- `text-transform` changes only **visually**. Copied text — original.
- `text-decoration: none` on `<a>` — link looks like plain text. Add `color`.

## Common mistake

`text-decoration: none` without a hover effect — links unrecognizable. Add `a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }`.

## Summary

- `text-decoration` — underline / none / line-through
- `text-transform` — case visually
- `white-space` — wrapping
- `text-shadow` — shadow

14.title: border and border-radius
14.theory:
## border

```css
.box {
  border: 1px solid black;
}
```

Three parts: **thickness** (px) + **style** + **color**.

## Styles

- `solid` — solid
- `dashed` — dashed
- `dotted` — dotted
- `double` — double
- `none` — remove

## Sides

```css
border-top: 2px solid red;
border-bottom: 1px dashed gray;
```

## border-radius

Rounding corners:

```css
.box { border-radius: 8px; }
.pill { border-radius: 999px; }  /* pill */
.circle { border-radius: 50%; }  /* circle if width == height */
```

## Individual corners

```css
border-top-left-radius: 10px;
border-radius: 10px 0 0 0;   /* only top-left */
```

Order: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.

## Circle

```css
.avatar {
  width: 80px;
  height: 80px;
  border-radius: 50%;
}
```

`50%` with equal sides = perfect circle.

## What if

- `border: solid` without thickness — not displayed.
- `border-radius: 50%` with different width/height — oval, not circle.

## Common mistake

`border: 1px black` without a style — does not work. Need style (`solid`).

## Summary

- `border: thickness style color`
- Styles: solid / dashed / dotted
- `border-radius` — rounding
- `50%` = circle

17.title: Flexbox: Container and Axes
17.theory:
## What flexbox is

A modern layout system. Lays out elements in a row/column with alignment.

## display: flex

On the **parent**:

```css
.row {
  display: flex;
}
```

All direct children become flex items, laid out in a row.

## Main and cross axes

- **main axis** — horizontal by default
- **cross axis** — vertical

## flex-direction

```css
.row { flex-direction: row; }          /* default: left to right */
.col { flex-direction: column; }       /* top to bottom */
.row-reverse { flex-direction: row-reverse; }
```

`column` — main axis is vertical.

## gap

Spacing between items:

```css
.row { gap: 10px; }
```

Modern way. Before — margin.

## What if

- `display: flex` on a child — does not work as expected. Flex — on the parent.
- `column` without `height` — container height by content.

## Common mistake

`gap` inside flex **does not work** in very old browsers. Now it is standard.

## Summary

- `display: flex` — on the parent
- `flex-direction` — row / column
- `gap` — spacing
- Main axis — direction of items

18.title: Flexbox: Alignment
18.theory:
## justify-content — main axis

```css
.row { justify-content: center; }
```

Values:
- `flex-start` — at start
- `flex-end` — at end
- `center` — center
- `space-between` — extremes at edges, gaps between
- `space-around` — around each
- `space-evenly` — equal gaps

## align-items — cross axis

```css
.row { align-items: center; }
```

- `flex-start` — top
- `flex-end` — bottom
- `center` — center
- `stretch` — stretch (default)
- `baseline` — by text baseline

## Example: center

```css
.center {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  align-items: center;
  height: 200px;
}
```

Perfect centering on both axes.

## flex-wrap

Wrap to a new line:

```css
.row { flex-wrap: wrap; }
```

Default — `nowrap` (all one line, squeezed).

## What if

- `align-items: center` without `height` — no visible effect, items of the same height.
- `wrap` without gap — items stick together.

## Common mistake

`justify-content: center` for **column** — centers vertically (main axis is different).

## Summary

- `justify-content` — main axis
- `align-items` — cross axis
- `center` + `center` + `height` = perfect center
- `flex-wrap: wrap` — wrap

19.title: Grid Basics
19.theory:
## What Grid is

CSS Grid — a two-dimensional grid. For layouts with both rows and columns.

## display: grid

```css
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 10px;
}
```

Three equal columns. `1fr` = one "fraction" (share).

## Repeat

```css
.grid {
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
}
```

Three equal columns. Shorter.

## What fr is

Fractional unit — a share of free space. `1fr 2fr` — second column twice as wide.

## auto-fit

```css
.grid {
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
}
```

Adaptive grid: as many columns as fit (min 200px). Modern magic.

## Grid vs Flexbox

- **Flexbox** — one-dimensional (row **or** column).
- **Grid** — two-dimensional (rows **and** columns).

For cards in a grid — Grid. For a menu — Flexbox.

## What if

- `display: grid` without `grid-template-columns` — one column.
- `1fr` without `gap` — cards stick together.

## Common mistake

`grid` for one-dimensional layout (menu) — overkill. Flexbox is simpler.

## Summary

- `display: grid` — two-dimensional
- `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` — three columns
- `1fr` — fraction
- `auto-fit` + `minmax` — adaptive
- Grid — for grids, Flexbox — for lines

20.title: position: static, relative, absolute
20.theory:
## position

The property defines how an element is positioned relative to others.

## static

Default. Normal flow. `top`, `left` etc. **do not work**.

## relative

```css
.box { position: relative; top: 10px; left: 20px; }
```

Offset from **its own place** in the flow. Its place **is kept** — neighbors do not move.

## absolute

```css
.parent { position: relative; }
.child { position: absolute; top: 10px; right: 10px; }
```

Positioned relative to the **nearest parent with position ≠ static**.

Important: the parent must have `position: relative` (or absolute / fixed), otherwise `absolute` flies to `<html>`.

## Out of flow

`absolute` is removed from the flow. Neighbors do not "see" it and may take its place.

## Example: badge in the corner

```css
.card { position: relative; }
.badge { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; }
```

## What if

- `absolute` without a `relative` parent — flies to the corner of `<body>`.
- `top` without `position` — does not work.

## Common mistake

`absolute` without `position: relative` on the parent. Most common issue.

## Summary

- `static` — normal
- `relative` — offset from own place
- `absolute` — from the nearest `relative` parent
- `absolute` — out of flow

options: From nearest parent with position ≠ static

21.title: position: fixed, sticky
21.theory:
## fixed

Pinned to the **browser window**:

```css
.nav { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; }
```

Stays in place on scroll. Often — for navigation, back-to-top button.

Out of flow — takes no space.

## sticky

A hybrid of `relative` and `fixed`:

```css
.header { position: sticky; top: 0; }
```

Behaves as `relative` until it reaches `top: 0`, then "sticks".

Handy for table headers, page headers.

## Sticky requirements

- Parent does not have `overflow: hidden` / `auto`
- Must have `top` (or other `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`)
- Parent is taller than the element — otherwise nowhere to stick

## fixed vs sticky

- **fixed** — always pinned to the window
- **sticky** — sticks on scroll up to the position

## What if

- `sticky` without `top` — does not work.
- `sticky` inside an `overflow: hidden` parent — does not work.

## Common mistake

`sticky` without `top/bottom/left/right`. Nowhere to "stick".

## Summary

- `fixed` — to window
- `sticky` — sticks on scroll
- `sticky` requires `top`
- fixed — out of flow / sticky — partially

22.title: z-index and Stacking
22.theory:
## Stacking

When elements overlap (via `absolute` or `fixed`), **z-index** decides — the "layer" along the Z axis.

## z-index

```css
.a { position: absolute; z-index: 1; }
.b { position: absolute; z-index: 10; }
```

`b` higher — larger number.

## Works only with position

`z-index` **does not work** for `position: static` (default). Need `relative`, `absolute`, `fixed` or `sticky`.

## DOM order

If `z-index` is equal, the element **later in HTML** is on top.

## Negative z-index

```css
.bg { position: absolute; z-index: -1; }
```

Goes under the parent. Careful — may go under the parent's background.

## Stacking context

A parent with `position: relative` + `z-index` creates its own context. Children cannot "jump" above elements **outside** this parent, even with a huge z-index.

## What if

- `z-index: 999` without `position` — does not work.
- Nested stacking contexts — z-index does not break through.

## Common mistake

`z-index: 9999` without `position`. Most common "does not work".

## Summary

- `z-index` — layer order
- Works only with `position ≠ static`
- Larger number — on top
- Stacking context limits

23.title: Units: px, %, em, rem
23.theory:
## Absolute

- `px` — pixels. Fixed. Independent of scale.

```css
.box { width: 200px; }
```

## Relative

- `%` — from parent
- `em` — from **parent** `font-size` (or current element)
- `rem` — from **root** (`<html>`) `font-size`
- `vw` / `vh` — % of window width / height

## rem vs em

```css
html { font-size: 16px; }
.a { font-size: 2rem; }   /* 32px (from html) */
.b { font-size: 1em; }    /* depends on parent */
```

`rem` — predictable. `em` — nested, can be surprising.

## vw / vh

```css
.hero { height: 100vh; }   /* full window height */
```

Useful for "above the fold". On mobile `vh` = height **with** the address bar (buggy). Modern solution — `dvh` (dynamic viewport).

## When what

- **px** — thin borders, shadows, exact sizes
- **rem** — fonts, spacing (scales)
- **%** — adaptive widths
- **vw/vh** — full screen

## What if

- `font-size: 20` without units — error.
- `%` for height without a parent `height` — 0.

## Common mistake

`font-size: 20` without units. In CSS explicitly `px` / `rem` / `em`.

## Summary

- `px` — fixed
- `rem` — from `<html>`
- `em` — from parent
- `%` — from parent
- `vw/vh` — window
- Fonts — in `rem`

26.title: transition
26.theory:
## What transition is

A smooth change of a property over time. Instead of an instant "before/after" — intermediate states.

```css
.btn {
  background: gray;
  transition: background 0.3s ease;
}
.btn:hover {
  background: blue;
}
```

On hover — smooth gray to blue over 0.3 seconds.

## Syntax

```css
transition: property duration timing-function delay;
```

- `property` — what changes
- `duration` — how long (0.3s, 300ms)
- `timing-function` — ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out
- `delay` — delay before start

## Multiple properties

```css
.btn {
  transition: background 0.3s ease, color 0.2s linear;
}
```

Or `all`:

```css
.btn { transition: all 0.3s ease; }
```

`all` — convenient but can be slower. Prefer explicit.

## Timing functions

- `ease` — slow-fast-slow (default)
- `linear` — uniform
- `ease-in` — slow at start
- `ease-out` — slow at end
- `ease-in-out` — slow at both ends
- `cubic-bezier(...)` — custom curve

## What animates

Not everything. `background`, `color`, `opacity`, `transform`, `width`, `height` — yes. `display` — no (instant).

`display: none` → `display: block` — no transition. Needs hacks.

## What if

- `transition: background` without `duration` — instant, useless.
- `transition: all 0.3s` — all properties, including unwanted.
- `transition` on `display` — does not work.

## Common mistake

Forgetting `transition` on the **base** rule, not on `:hover`. Transition must be on base for both directions.

## Summary

- `transition: property duration timing delay`
- Multiple — comma-separated
- `all` — everything
- Does not work on `display`
- On the base rule, not `:hover`

27.title: transform
27.theory:
## What transform is

Geometric changes: translation, rotation, scaling. Does not affect flow — neighbors stay put.

## Basic functions

```css
.box { transform: translateX(20px); }
.box { transform: scale(1.2); }
.box { transform: rotate(45deg); }
.box { transform: skew(10deg); }
```

## translate

```css
transform: translate(x, y);
transform: translateX(20px);
transform: translateY(-10px);
transform: translate(50%, 50%);
```

## scale

```css
transform: scale(2);
transform: scale(1.5, 0.5);
```

Scales **from center** by default.

## rotate

```css
transform: rotate(45deg);
```

Clockwise. `-45deg` — counter-clockwise.

## Multiple functions

```css
transform: translate(10px, 20px) rotate(45deg) scale(1.2);
```

Space-separated. Order **matters** — applied sequentially.

## transform-origin

```css
.box { transform-origin: top left; }
```

`center` by default.

## Transition + transform

```css
img { transition: transform 0.3s ease; }
img:hover { transform: scale(1.05); }
```

## What if

- `rotate` without `deg` — does not work.
- Forget `transform-origin` — rotate from center, not corner.
- Wrong order: `rotate(45) translate(20)` ≠ `translate(20) rotate(45)`.

## Common mistake

`transform: rotate(45)` without `deg`. Units are mandatory.

## Summary

- `translate` — shift
- `scale` — scale
- `rotate` — rotate
- Space-separated, order matters
- `transform-origin` — anchor
- Smooth — via `transition`

## Why When you need styles not for all elements, but for specific ones by position or excluding some. ## :first-child and :last-child ```css li:first-child { font-weight: bold; } li:last-child { border-bottom: none; } ``` First and last. ## :nth-child(n) ```css li:nth-child(2) { color: red; } li:nth-child(odd) { background: #eee; } li:nth-child(even) { background: #fff; } li:nth-child(3n) { color: blue; } li:nth-child(2n+1) { font-weight: bold; } ``` ## :not(selector) ```css li:not(:last-child) { border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc; } button:not(.primary) { background: gray; } ``` All elements **except** the specified ones. ## :first-of-type / :last-of-type Similar to `:first-child`, but works within **type**: ```css p:first-of-type { font-size: 1.2em; } ``` First `

` in parent — even if `

` is before. ## :nth-of-type(n) ```css p:nth-of-type(2) { color: red; } ``` Second `

`, regardless of other tags. ## What if - `li:nth-child(2)` — not "second `li`", but "element that is second child and `li`". If second is `

`, style does not apply. - `:not(.a.b)` — error, `:not` does not accept complex selectors in older browsers. ## Common mistake `:nth-child(2)` on `
  • `, but with `

    ` between `li` — the `li` that is second among all is not the second `li`. Need `:nth-of-type(2)`. ## Summary - `:first-child`, `:last-child` — first/last - `:nth-child(n)` — by count - `odd` / `even` — odds/evens - `:not(sel)` — exclusion - `-of-type` — only own type

32.title: filter and @font-face
32.theory:
## filter

Visual effects:

```css
img { filter: grayscale(100%); }
.box { filter: blur(4px); }
.btn { filter: brightness(1.2); }
```

- `blur(px)` — blur
- `brightness(x)` — brightness (1 = normal)
- `contrast(x)` — contrast
- `grayscale(x)` — B&W (1 = fully)
- `sepia(x)` — sepia
- `saturate(x)` — saturation
- `hue-rotate(deg)` — hue shift
- `drop-shadow(...)` — shadow

## Multiple filters

```css
img {
  filter: grayscale(0.5) brightness(1.1);
}
```

Space-separated.

## Use cases

- B&W image until hover, color on hover.
- "Loading" effect via blur.
- Shadow for PNG with transparency — `drop-shadow`.

## @font-face

Loading a custom font:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: 'MyFont';
  src: url('font.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-weight: normal;
}

body {
  font-family: 'MyFont', sans-serif;
}
```

`src` — file path. `format` — type.

## Formats

- `woff2` — modern, compressed
- `woff` — older, wider support
- `ttf`, `otf` — large, for desktop

`woff2` — priority.

## Google Fonts

Alternative — ready fonts via `<link>`:

```html
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto" rel="stylesheet">
```

```css
body { font-family: 'Roboto', sans-serif; }
```

## What if

- `filter` on a huge image — lag
- `@font-face` without `format` — browser may not load
- Font not loaded — fallback

## Common mistake

Forget `font-family` in `@font-face` — font not activated.

## Summary

- `filter: grayscale(1)` — effects
- Multiple — space-separated
- `@font-face` — own font
- `woff2` — format
- Fallback mandatory
